name: yoast
notes: DUO-3223 boundary certification: the official WordPress.org releases are pinned by exact SHA-256 at the real in-range edges 28.0 (the manifest's inclusive minimum, spelled exactly like the plugin header because PHP version_compare() orders 28.0 below 28.0.0) and 28.3 (the current stable below 29.0.0), plus 27.9 as the closest stable below-range refusal control. The matrix installs only those verified artifacts, proves a real in-place 28.0 to 28.3 upgrade as well as a fresh 28.3 target, exercises Yoast's own authored APIs and rendered output, and never substitutes a latest-slug install. Yoast 28.0 lazily replaces wpseo_titles.company_logo_meta=false with a deterministic image-metadata object on first frontend render; the seed deliberately warms that render before capture and the nested company_logo_meta.id is declared as a post reference below, preventing the source-local attachment id from leaking into canonical state or appearing as post-apply drift.

DUO-3222 (version-pinned adapter compatibility contract): plugin/version_range verified live (not guessed) — wordpress-seo/wp-seo.php, re-confirmed at exact 28.3 this session. Range scoped to the CURRENT major line only (28.x, [28.0, 29.0.0)) — widening to cover other major versions is DUO-3224's ratification job, not invented here.

wpseo_titles/wpseo_social logo/default-social-image sub-keys: CLOSED (task #31 — was the KNOWN GAP this note used to describe). Real key names verified empirically on a running install (e1, Yoast SEO 28.2), not trusted from memory: wpseo_titles.company_logo_id / wpseo_titles.person_logo_id / wpseo_social.og_default_image_id — spelled exactly as originally guessed here, but their STORAGE TYPE was not, and reading actual bytes caught a real divergence: company_logo_id and person_logo_id are native PHP ints both unset (`i:0;`, class-wpseo-option-titles.php's own defaults) and set (`i:12;` after WPSEO_Options::set(), which routes through the same sanitize_option_wpseo_titles filter — hence the same WPSEO_Utils::validate_int() — a genuine wp-admin settings save would hit). og_default_image_id is native-int too ONCE SET (`i:14;`), but its UNSET default is a literal empty STRING (`s:0:"";`, class-wpseo-option-social.php's own default table) — it only becomes an int the first time a real value is saved (validate_option(): `$clean[$key] = ($dirty[$key] === '') ? $dirty[$key] : (int) $dirty[$key];`). This is NOT the digit-string shape wpseo_taxonomy_meta's wpseo_opengraph-image-id/wpseo_twitter-image-id siblings use below — assuming the same cast:"string" here by analogy would have been wrong; empirical bytes-before-and-after (not the taxonomy-meta precedent) settled it. All three get plain `json_refs` (kind:post, no cast — the native-int type is exactly what json_refs/Tokens restores by default on apply). Their plain-URL siblings (company_logo/person_logo/og_default_image) needed no separate declaration: the moment an option has ANY json_refs, Tokens::struct_capture()'s whole-structure string-leaf pass (the same free ride wpseo_taxonomy_meta's other fields already get) tokenizes every remaining string leaf automatically — verified round-trip on e1 (uploads-relative URL -> `{{uploads}}/...` -> byte-restored on apply). Two sibling fields with the identical id+url shape were noticed in passing but are deliberately NOT declared here — out of this task's named scope, and not exercised by any conformance seed, so a rule for them would be exactly the untested guess this project's discipline exists to avoid: `open_graph_frontpage_image_id` (wpseo_titles — front-page-specific OG image override; shares company_logo_id/person_logo_id's own validate_option() switch-case, so almost certainly native-int too, but not confirmed by setting a real value) and `og_frontpage_image_id` (wpseo_social — the frontpage-override twin of og_default_image_id, same empty-string-until-set shape observed for its sibling). Left for a future pass alongside wpseo_rss/wpseo_internallinks/wpseo_xml below. Seeded going forward by conformance/seeds/yoast.sh (three attachments — company logo, person logo, OG default image — set via WPSEO_Options::set(), the same real API used for wpseo_taxonomy_meta's own seed). Two corrections to this note's own prior text, caught by deliberately reverting this fix and re-capturing/re-linting rather than trusting the old wording: first, with no ref/json_refs at all, an array-shaped option (which is exactly what wpseo_titles/wpseo_social unserialize to) is captured as a raw NESTED OBJECT in canonical state, not a 'plain whole-value string' as previously written here — and every field inside it, ids and URLs alike, is left completely untokenized (confirmed: reverting produced `"company_logo": "http://localhost:8804/wp-content/uploads/..."` in state/options/core.json, a live environment hostname, not just the three bare ids). Second, `wp duo lint`'s bare_id class DOES see a sub-key nested one level inside an undeclared option value — its shallow scan checks the DIRECT CHILDREN of the whole option value, and company_logo_id/person_logo_id/og_default_image_id are exactly one level deep — reverting this fix and re-running capture+lint reproduced precisely three bare_id findings, one per sub-key, each correctly resolved to its real attachment (`options.wpseo_titles[company_logo_id]` -> #12, `options.wpseo_titles[person_logo_id]` -> #13, `options.wpseo_social[og_default_image_id]` -> #14) — `wp duo capture` itself even surfaces a live 'N suspicious unrewritten ref(s)' warning at capture time, not only via a separate lint invocation. The gap was real (nothing tokenized these fields), but it went unexercised rather than undetectable: no conformance seed had ever configured a logo/image, so lint had nothing to flag. A json_refs-declared structure's DEEPER positions (two-plus levels down, e.g. wpseo_taxonomy_meta's shape below) are the case the shallow scan genuinely cannot reach without a declaration triggering scan_structured_bare_ids' deep walk.

wpseo (the main options blob) as a WHOLE remains deliberately uncaptured: mixes genuine feature toggles with env-local bookkeeping (`first_activated_on`/`first_activated_by`/`activation_redirect_timestamp_free` timestamps, `indexing_started`/`indexing_reason` one-shot install state, `version`/`previous_version` Yoast's own upgrade-routine gate, per-environment integration tokens like `semrush_tokens`/`wincher_tokens`). Capturing it wholesale would let a stale captured version silently roll back another environment's upgrade-routine gate. DUO-3233 closed the underlying engine gap ('v0's options model has no sub-key split to capture only the safe half' — no longer true, see Policy::sub_keyed_options()), and this manifest now carves out ONE real, empirically-verified, unambiguous toggle as the second proof of that grammar beyond Polylang's `polylang` option (this manifest's OWN identical shape was cited by DUO-3233's own problem statement): `disableadvanced_meta` (Yoast SEO 28.2, live install, not guessed — a plain boolean, 'Disable the advanced part of the meta box', a genuine wp-admin content-authoring preference with no ids/secrets/env-bound shape whatsoever). Verified live: capturing/applying it merges cleanly into the target's OWN `wpseo` blob without touching `version`/`first_activated_on`/any of the ~115 other sibling keys. The other ~100+ keys in this option (many of them plausibly safe, e.g. `enable_admin_bar_menu`/`enable_xml_sitemap`/the `remove_feed_*` family) are deliberately NOT classified here — same 'do NOT guess' discipline as wpseo_rss/wpseo_internallinks/wpseo_xml below: a full `wpseo` sub-key audit is real, separate, future work, not attempted in this task's scope.

wpseo_taxonomy_meta now captured authored (task #11 wave 2 closed this gap): PHP-serialized `{taxonomy_name: {term_id: {...fields...}}}` (verified empirically via WPSEO_Taxonomy_Meta::set_values(), Yoast's own documented public API — not guessed; term_id keys are genuinely PHP int-typed, e.g. `i:13;`, not strings). key_refs (`{"path": "$.*", "kind": "term"}`) rewrites the per-taxonomy submap's term-id KEYS through the ledger; json_refs rewrites the two id-VALUED sibling fields the same $defaults_per_term array declares (wpseo_opengraph-image-id / wpseo_twitter-image-id, both stored as digit STRINGS — `s:2:"11"` — hence cast:"string" on both paths, preserving the exact serialized type on apply). Every other field (wpseo_desc, wpseo_noindex, the plain-URL wpseo_opengraph-image/wpseo_twitter-image siblings, ...) is tokenize_text()'d automatically by the same whole-structure string-leaf pass json_refs/key_refs values always get — no path needed for those. Round-trips proven end-to-end (fx1/fx2, genuine term-id and attachment-id divergence, raw DB byte inspection both sides) and lint-clean both directions (declared paths clean; an undeclared image-id path, tested by deliberately dropping it, is precisely flagged and doesn't false-positive on the correctly-token-keyed term entry it lives inside).

wpseo_rss/wpseo_internallinks/wpseo_xml look like safe, config-heavy candidates for a future pass; left undeclared (uncaptured, never blocking) here rather than classified from memory without empirical verification against a running install.

rebuilder verified against a running install: 'wp yoast index' takes its OWN --skip-confirmation flag for non-interactive use, not the generic wp-cli --yes (confirmed empirically — --yes is rejected as an unknown parameter). Separately, and unrelated to that flag: since Yoast SEO 15.1, indexable creation is production-only by design (gated on wp_get_environment_type() === 'production', bypassable only via the Yoast\WP\SEO\should_index_indexables filter) — every sandbox/CI env here runs WP_ENVIRONMENT_TYPE=local, so this rebuilder is expected to warn-not-fail (Apply's rebuild pass treats rebuilder exit != 0 as a warning) in every environment this repo's tests ever run against, and will only actually index on a real production site. Not a bug; do not silence the warning by defining the override filter in the agent — that would change Yoast's own behavior underneath every site, production included, which is Yoast's call to make per-site, not Duo's to make globally.

DUO-3338 (structured actions supersede the free-form `rebuilders` channel): `yoast index --reindex --skip-confirmation` is now provider `yoast-index` capability `reindex` (manifests/providers/yoast-index.php), which still invokes that plugin-owned CLI command and stays unscoped as the declaration was. Two corrections to the note below, which described engine behavior that has since changed: a failing rebuild has been a hard apply failure since DUO-3206, not a warning, and this capability additionally verifies value-level — a non-zero wp_yoast_indexable row count when public posts exist AND the environment type is 'production' (the only case Yoast 15.1+ indexes at all; elsewhere the receipt records the no-op branch explicitly, per the production-only gate the note below documents) — so neither a non-zero exit nor a silently empty production index can pass.

Production-readiness closure updates yoast-index to provider identity 2.0.0. Exact 28.3 source proves the command writes four derived tables, not two: Index_Command truncates yoast_indexable and yoast_indexable_hierarchy, Indexable_Builder invokes Primary_Term_Builder for yoast_primary_term, and the post/term link actions write yoast_seo_links. The provider now schema-checks all four before the destructive command, uses Yoast's own should_index_indexables() answer rather than guessing from environment type alone, and verifies public-post coverage, primary-term ownership, hierarchy integrity, and SEO-link completion. Its action is trigger-bounded and checkpoints the four tables plus options because the command also mutates Yoast's indexation-complete option/transients.

yoast_expiring_store (round-3 T7 A4, Yoast SEO 28.2 live on the adoption pair): a TTL key/value cache store (key_name PK, value, exp) Yoast added in the 28.x line and creates on activation, empty on a fresh site. Pure per-environment runtime, the same class Action Scheduler's tables carry in manifests/woocommerce.json — undeclared it surfaced as table:yoast_expiring_store unclassified and blocked the first release of a Yoast site with release_surface_not_releasable until an operator classified it by hand.

wpseo_llmstxt (DUO-3509): Yoast 28.3's llms.txt settings, one of three names a fresh `duo init` demanded a decision for on WP 7.0.3 + Yoast 28.3. Grounded by reading WPSEO_Option_Llmstxt directly (inc/options/class-wpseo-option-llmstxt.php), not from the settings screen: the persisted blob is exactly the six keys its own `$defaults` names — llms_txt_selection_mode ('auto'|'manual'), about_us_page, contact_page, terms_page, privacy_policy_page, shop_page (ints, 0 when unset) and other_included_pages (a LIST of ints, capped at WPSEO_Option_Llmstxt::OTHER_INCLUDED_PAGES_LIMIT = 100). It is exactly six because WPSEO_Option::validate() starts from `$clean = $this->get_defaults()` (inc/options/class-wpseo-option.php:494) and this option declares no variable_array_key_patterns, so no other key survives a save; a key removed from the row is re-filled from the same defaults on read (:744, `array_merge($defaults, $options)`). Every page key is a post reference: validate_option()'s about_us_page/contact_page/terms_page/privacy_policy_page/shop_page case runs WPSEO_Utils::validate_int() and keeps `$int >= 0`, and the other_included_pages case validates each array item the same way, skipping 0/false. Declared with sub_keys rather than `class: authored` + json_refs, and that shape is load-bearing rather than stylistic: other_included_pages is a list of SCALARS, and JsonRefs cannot address it — `$.other_included_pages` resolves to the container, which StructuredReferenceCodec::capture() skips outright ('A declared path resolved to a container, not a scalar id', agent/src/Kernel/StructuredReferenceCodec.php:38), while `$.other_included_pages.*` matches nothing at all because JsonRefs' transparent array mapping re-applies the same segment to each element and step() returns immediately on a non-array node. A sub-key rule is a whole option rule one nesting level down (OptionsCapture::capture_value() / OptionsMaterializer::apply_value() dispatch json_refs/key_refs/ref/plain-string identically for it), so `ref: post[]` — the same rule core.json's sticky_posts uses — is available there and is the only correct expression of this field. The 0-means-unset convention needs no special handling: option_ref_tokens() returns null for a scalar 0 (OptionsCapture.php:391-394) and skips 0 elements inside a `[]` ref (:375-379), so an unset page is captured as the sub-key's ABSENCE, and DUO-3264's sub-key tombstone then removes that key from the target's live blob on apply, where Yoast re-fills it from $defaults on the next read. Parent class `env, required: false` follows this manifest's own `wpseo` shape and polylang.json's `polylang`: the parent class governs only keys this manifest has NOT carved out, and `duo env-set` refuses a sub_keys-bearing env option by name rather than treating it as a provisioning slot (ApplyRequestCoordinator.php:514-520, 559-561). Today there are no such keys — the six above are the whole blob — so the parent class is a declaration about what a FUTURE Yoast key would default to, not about anything currently excluded.

wpseo_tracking_only / yoast_migrations_free (DUO-3509): the other two names that fresh install surfaced, both runtime, both verified in Yoast 28.3's source. wpseo_tracking_only holds exactly three timestamps — task_list_first_opened_on, task_first_actioned_on, frontend_inspector_first_actioned_on (inc/options/class-wpseo-option-tracking-only.php) — whose own class docblock says their 'only purpose is tracking' and whose validate_option() enforces write-once semantics ('These should be set only once and never changed again'), keeping the old value against any later change. Per-environment telemetry about when someone first opened a screen HERE; carrying a source's timestamps onto a target would assert an interaction that never happened there, and the write-once rule means the target could not correct it. yoast_migrations_free is Yoast's own migration-runner state, named `Migration_Status::MIGRATION_OPTION_KEY . $name` = 'yoast_migrations_' + 'free' (src/config/migration-status.php:17; the 'free' migration set is registered in src/generated/container.php). Runtime rather than env — where this manifest's own `tables.yoast_migrations` and woocommerce.json's `woocommerce_db_version` sit — because it is not a version marker: alongside `version` the same array carries `lock`, a live ten-minute mutex timestamp written by lock_migration() and honoured by should_run_migration() ('Check if we've attempted to run this migration in the past 10 minutes. If so, it may still be running'), and `error`, a per-run failure record with its own `time` written by set_error(). Replaying another environment's row would either roll back this environment's upgrade gate — the exact hazard this manifest's `wpseo` note already records for `version`/`previous_version` — or hand it a foreign lock/error, which is the same class of live mutex WooCommerce's wc_installing carries (see manifests/woocommerce.json's own DUO-3509 note).
